result.title: Shaping & Monitoring Models through their Internal Representations
result.summary: We propose Mechanistic Shaping, a unified framework for shaping models through their internal representations. Mechanistic Shaping is applied during training so that models follow specifications (rules) about which concepts they express, measured via their outputs or internal representations (e.g., no harmful content), and also which concepts they rely on, i.e., what they use to make their decisions (e.g., not a candidate's gender when screening a résumé). Across multiple domains (vision, medical imaging, language), scales (up to 32B parameters), and training paradigms (classification, SFT, DPO, GRPO), we find that Mechanistic Shaping substantially reduces targeted behaviors while preserving task performance. Since training against a representation can also modify it, we ask whether shaped concepts remain monitorable, a question that depends on the class of monitors considered. We therefore introduce a hierarchy of such classes, which separates a concept that escapes one probe from a concept that is truly gone. We characterize three geometric mechanisms of circumvention: the concept can drift away from the monitor, be erased from the layer, or persist in higher-order statistics as a nonlinear encoding, which we explain through a product-code construction. Although other mechanisms may arise in different settings or at larger scales, these three account for all of our observations, and each can be detected by a matching monitor. In practice, we find that shaped concepts largely remain monitorable: refitted linear probes recover the concept in most settings, and the original probe remains reliable whenever gradients do not flow through it. Taken together, these results point to the potential of using interpretability as a tool for training, and call for a correspondingly rigorous science of interpretability-based training.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Mechanistic Shaping 训练框架，通过输出或内部表示约束模型表达及依赖的概念，在视觉、医学影像、语言、最高 32B 及分类/SFT/DPO/GRPO 上验证；并给出监控器层级与概念规避的三种几何机制（漂移、擦除、非线性高阶编码）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其区分「逃出某个探针」与「概念真正消失」的层级、重拟合探针与梯度隔离实验，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 是否真实保留视觉内容、线性探针读数的可信度及信息坍缩判定，迁移到多模态推理尚需较多验证。
